_comment: REFERENCE — every key the script reads, in one file, so you can see what
is available. To start a repo off, copy the closest file from templates/
instead; this one turns everything on at once.
Every key is optional — create-worktree auto-detects Docker, nginx and the
database, and skips whatever it cannot find. A repo with no Dockerfile gets
just a worktree plus symlinks.
The values below are quarterback's, but note that quarterback's real
.worktree.json (repo root) sets docker.enabled=false and does not pin the
Postgres container — because its docker-compose.yml is tracked in git and
the Docker path would overwrite it. Read that file too.
base_port is 5690, not 5681: the main compose stack already publishes 5681
for the app, and allocating from there hands the first worktree a port it
cannot bind. Start yours above every port your own compose file publishes.
database.protect is a list of GLOB patterns naming databases prune-worktrees
must never call orphans. Use it for databases your project generates on some
axis other than the worktree -- per-migration-head test templates being the
usual one, which is why the value below is a wildcard rather than a name: a
hand-pinned head is stale the next time somebody lands a migration, and it is
stale silently. A literal entry still works, since a pattern with no
metacharacters matches exactly. See harness/README.md, `Databases the sweep
must not touch`.
That one is ILLUSTRATIVE and not quarterback's: this repo mints no template
databases, so its real .worktree.json sets no protect list at all. The shape
is what to copy, not the string.
